title: Product in motion
rationale: The commerce case for video: start from an approved product shot and move it, without the label, shape or colour drifting. A product that changes between frames cannot run as an ad.
prompt: Using the supplied product shot as the first frame, a hand enters, picks the product up, turns it to show the side, and sets it down. The product's shape, label and colour must not change at any point.

variants.prompt: Using the supplied product shot as the first frame, the camera orbits a quarter turn around the product. The product stays identical; only the viewing angle changes.
Using the supplied product shot as the first frame, water splashes over the product and runs off it. The label stays legible and unchanged.
Using the supplied product shot as the first frame, two hands lift the product out of a plain cardboard box and set it on the box lid. The product does not change.
Using the supplied product shot as the first frame, the camera pulls back from the product to reveal it on a shop shelf among other items. The product does not change.

rubric: Is the product unchanged in shape, label and colour in every frame?
Does frame one match the supplied product shot?
Is the motion physically plausible, hands included?
Could a brand run this as an ad without fixes?
